review:
TLDR: A twin-stick shooter with satisfying gameplay and fantastic soundtrack. Devs understand how to make a good arcade game with high difficulty and no bs concentrated intense gaming. Achievements encourage you to learn the game and face harder challenges: felt very rewarding completing 100%. Totally worth it playing!
   An arcade game the way it should be: no time to explain – grab the gun and shoot the enemies. Clear visuals: everything is distinct and easy to parse. Controls are responsive and fluid – feels satisfying to move and shoot. However, you can’t reassign buttons and are forced to play with predetermined scheme. Playing with keyboard is probably not the best idea – the binds are quite unintuitive, so I played with a controller, and, although I probably would change a few buttons, it was no problem. As for music and sound, their volume is a binary switch: I would certainly like a slider. Good thing is - they are awesome! There are not many game osts which I would listen away from the game itself, but this is absolutely such a case. Sounds are juicy and the announcer approaches “heavy machinegun” levels – pure bliss. 
   Jumping doesn’t give you i-frames, so it’s used for movement and reposition purposes. However you can damage certain enemies while rolling at them. It’s dangerous, but provides opportunities for skill play. Another aspect of combat is melee: it’s rather risky, but once you learn to use it, it feels rewarding and sometimes gives you an advantage. Most weapon pickups are either a huge straight-up power boost, or might be a bit finicky but very potent in certain spots, however it seems like homing is almost always a downgrade – it could definitely use a buff.
   Dog tags are a pickup used to make purchases in the shop. It doesn’t introduce power imbalance, however I’m not sure it’s really needed. You can generally upgrade important stats like dmg, hp and speed pretty quickly. For example, already after level 1 you can get your damage to max. It kinda works, as there are no meta upgrades and everything is contained within one run, however after about level 5 (of 7) there is no point in picking up dogtags: you’ll be maxed out on upgrades, which looks like a design flaw – there is no other way to utilize currency. You could buy continue pills, but we don’t talk about those here ;) So the shop system isn’t a detriment, but could be more deep and nuanced.
   Each level consists of a chain of rooms: once you enter, you are locked inside until all aliens are cleared. Enemies do not pile up: if you stop killing, new ones won’t spawn. This prevents frustrating experiences, when falling behind might snowball you into a very bad situation, however I wonder if enemy cap could be significantly increased on a hard difficulty setting. Your base gun has finite ammo, however, once you run out, a pickup will appear, which tops it up: this gives incentives not to shoot all the time. There is basically no backtracking: in some levels you have to move to a side room to get a key to progress, but it doesn’t waste your time. 
   The game is really challenging in a good way: it’s not purposefully unfair or impossible even for a not so skilled player like me, but challenging enough that you can’t beat it by chance. It took me 23,5 hours to beat the game on base difficulty and it felt very rewarding. Even the way they name it “easy” pokes you and incentivizes to push further. So, naturally I went for a hard mode. Enemy hp remain the same, but they move faster and projectile speed increases, so it makes it more challenging without turning enemies into bullet sponges. For my taste, they could make it a bit harder in some aspects: like higher enemy cap, more shooting enemies, but it’s still challenging as is. At a 36,5h mark I managed to beat hard mode. 
   Achievements push you to take on harder challenges, while not forcing to engage in unfun gameplay patterns. For example, getting 200 dogtags means you can spend very little in shop, so it’s akin to low% run. Usually not a fan of coop achievements, but you can easily do it solo. When doing S-grades on individual levels, you can get hit no more than once – I appreciate that you have a small amount of leeway here: it’s still hard, but the devs meet you halfway. Well, more like 5%-way:) To do it in a sane way, you need to level select – you get the code after beating the game. I almost gave up on getting S in HQ until I learned that you can fight the boss if you access it from backers menu (not the cheat menu) Last level is brutal, even on easy when you go for S-grade. Took me 61,5h to complete all the achievements and the journey felt amazing.
   Scoring: I’m just a normie-survival player, but I’ll try to elaborate nevertheless. First, there are no leaderboards. To compare and compete against other players is the whole point! They did consider a few things for the scoring system though: additional points for picking hp and grenades when maxed out, which gives incentives to not get hit and not use powerful grenades. The presence of optional rooms in some levels provides additional opportunities to increase your score, but bears risks, which is a proper dynamics. Melee gives double the points too. As far as I know, you can’t milk for points. So, there is foundation, but devs didn’t lead idea to its conclusion. Simply adding scoring “because arcade game” is not very thoughtful: ideally scoring system is integrated within the game process itself and gives it depth. Even in sonic every 50k would give you 1 life, so it was vaguely connected to gameplay and you would get big bonuses for finishing level fast - nothing of the sort here. At the end of a game, which usually takes 35-40 min to beat, you are shown your time, rank and kills. Seeing how you are always evaluated on your performance via a rank system, I would like more though and transparency put into it. For example, why not include a menu section, which shows requirements for each rank as well as how you can score more points. You could also get big bonuses for, let’s say flawless level, more point for not using bombs at the end of a level etc. That’s a loss of good opportunity to enrich the game.
   You can select between two characters but the difference is purely cosmetic. I’d enjoy having meaningfully different chars, but it’s fine.
   Boss fights provide a change of pace each with unique soundtrack and mechanics; however they are way too easy. Also, very minor changes between easy and hard mode: don’t like it - I think they should be scaled way more for hard difficulty: more hp and certainly more aggression, bullets and new attack patterns. There is boss rush, which was helpful in practicing against final boss.
   There is a survival mode with non-stop action without transitioning to rooms – this is a fun way to practice and challenge yourself. The shop upgrades work as pickups here, so there is variance in the order and types of powerups you get. Personally, I didn’t get to 2500 kills, even though I got an achievement for doing so. I think the way the game treats it is incorrect: you don’t have to get the kills during a single run, but rather it adds your results during a single game session. That’s what happened to me: I jammed several runs one by one, getting 800-1000 kills and then suddenly 2500 kills cheevo popped. Although I’ve gotten pretty close one time – to 2470 and choked at the very end :) Getting there is not trivial as rng, especially getting a rare full heal, is often the difference. Still a fun mode.
   The game is an easy recommend, despite its minor shortcomings, even if you don’t want to attempt all the achievements: simply beating it once is worth it - gameplay is involved and the music is fire. Xeno Crisis is hard, credit feed is discouraged and so seeing your improvements feels very fulfilling. I’m glad that games like that are still being made nowadays. Mission all over!

There is a reason this game is not talked about when mentioning modern Arcade classics, it's a very nice looking game with great music and a simple enough premise that should be difficult to mess up, but bizarre game choices and terrible controls killed it.

I played this game for more than 10 hours but since I did it in offline mode the total playtime didn't synch properly.
I don't know how where to start so I'll just make a list of the glaring problems with this game after spending way too much time on it.
-For some bizarre reason, your main weapon has limited ammo, but the game throws you an ammo box as soon as you're about to run out, why is this a problem? It brings the pace of the game to a halt. The ammo box might spawn too close to enemies, making it annoying and difficult to get back to shooting, this becomes a glaring issue on later levels, where enemies spawn by lots and they become bullet sponges, even when you're max upgraded on ammo and power this is still an issue.
-Bizarrely, the weapon pickups are temporary powerups, at the beginning of the game this might seem innofensive, but once you hit the midpoint, you'll realize what a terrible choice that is since you'll start encountering enemies that burrow, or jump, removing themselves from the arena and wasting precious time from your (for no reason) timed powerup, instead of making the main weapon have limited ammo, weapon pickups SHOULD have been the ones to need ammo, and having ammo pick ups appear to extend their duration could have been the choice, anything but timed.
-Weapon pickups balance is out of wack, rebound shot, and homing shot are terrible weapons and do more harm than good when picking them up, where ass the rest of the weapons like the laser, rocket launcher, and shotguns are just good at any time, Seems like the developers realized this so the only quality of life feature this game has is that you can discard your weapon power up, thank god.
-Enemy bullets are small and hard to see, they're yellow like your own bullets, so it can even get more lost if the shot happens to align with your bullet's trail. You'll end up losing health from bullets you will not be able to see coming, it doesn't feel good.
-Some enemies shoot as soon as they spawn, like some walking red aliens from area 2, since spawns are random there is nothing you can do to prepare for this but always expect the worst and play too careful, which is not fun, that's the problem, there is no tell, no animation, no anything, you can't react.
-Some enemies will spawn under your feet and you will lose precious health, feels terrible and unfair, this never got fixed since the game's release, it's insane.
-If you use 1 continue you're locked out of the good ending, that would be reasonable in other games maybe, but not in this game where losing health can just randomly happen.
-Your melee attack absolutely SUCKS, the range is small, and the animation is unsatisfying, and enemies do contact damage so most of the time you'll lose health to the enemy you just killed with your melee attack, easily one of the worst melee attacks in a game I have played.
-Your dodge roll is terrible, the range is so weird too, it's really hard to measure the distance of it so you'll end up rolling into an enemy or a bullet, might as well just not use it.
-Item pickups like tags, grenades, or health are on a timer too, wouldn't be an issue if they didn't spawn between enemies, so you have to deal with bullet sponge enemies, small bullets you can barely see, and a really small timer to be able to pick this stuff up, tags are necessary to level up your character, so it's not something you can just forego, same for health, you will NEED those pickups.

There is probably more but it's all I can think of from the top of my head right now.

This game would have been an absolute hit back in the 90s, but sadly it didn’t manage to hold my attention in today's gaming landscape.

The difficulty feels more punishing than fun, especially if you just want to enjoy it casually with a friend on the couch. Sure, with enough persistence you could push through, but it doesn’t really feel rewarding or engaging.

The controls are stuck in the past, limited to 8 directions instead of offering smooth, free aiming. It had the potential to be a modern take on classics like Smash TV, but instead, it feels more frustrating than fun.

Variety is limited, enemies get increasingly unfair, and the upgrades you unlock after each level barely make a difference during gameplay.

Overall, I can’t really recommend it, especially considering the price. It feels more like something that would fit as a fun little side game in a collection like UFO 50, rather than a standalone title.

Xenocrisis is an action packed twin stick arena shooter heavily inspired by Smash TV and 90's Sci-Fi movies.  The pixel art is absolutely fantastic.  I love the retro gameplay and fun boss fights.  This game clearly understands what it's influences are, and why they were great, and mashes them all up into a fun little package.  The problem is that with the low rez pixelated graphics enemy projectiles often blend into the background.  Overall, the difficulty is moderate and fun.  However, it is brutally punishing to get hit with so many projectiles you just cant see on screen.  There is so much action going on, that you will be hit by things you were too distracted to see, and that feels legitimate and fair.  It's the attacks you cant see the really bring this game down.  I wish the projectiles had some kind of lighting effect or a higher contrast to make them stand out from the great pixel art backgrounds more.  Overall this is an amazing game with a serious flaw.  I'm going to recommend it, but with a serious caviot about the enemy bullets.

[h3] CRISIS DE XENOS [/h3]

- Un Twin-Stick shooter arcade de los viejos tiempos muy parecido a Smash TV pero con la temática Alien que es todavia mejor de a dos jugadores.
- Un control que a pesar de sus problemas es divertido de dominar, con un salto, granada y ataque melee.
- Los gráficos pixelados con la paleta y la onda Megadrive/Genesis son un golazo.... justamente porque es un juego de Sega pero del 2019 por lo que si te llama la atención recomiendo bajar su Rom para probar la version original en el emulador Kega fusion.
- Referencias a lo loco principalmente a Alien, Contra, Doom y Resident Evil
- Los enemigos tienen buen diseño y son todos odiosos. Matarlos es una liberación de estrés.
- La música es buena porque acompaña una banda, con todos los sonidos de los enemigos y armas pero el comandante es infumable.. el tipo literal dice "Salva a los humanos" que sos un alien salame? .
- El juego tiene una mecánica única que no vi en otros juegos, el arma tiene munición limitada por lo que al vaciarse aparece una caja para recargar. Esto le mete mas dificultad y te obliga a moverte por el mapa.

*Algunos detalles:
- El juego es bastante difícil, en sus dos dificultades, pero mas que nada por lo injusto, desde proyectiles del mismo color con un tamaño mínimo, enemigos que aparecen encima nuestro y el hitbox de nuestro personaje que es inmenso.
- Los jefes tienen un diseño espectacular, pero son muy simples ya que tienen 2 patrones con suerte y el jefe final es pedorro.
- Repetitivo y Alargado de mas, cada partida lleva 40 minutos donde se recicla muchísimos elementos como enemigos, niveles con diseños pocos destacables y los últimos 3 fases son las mas largas y llenas de enemigos molestos que para colmo son esponjas de daño.
- Recomiendo jugar en difícil porque hace mas entretenido el dominarlo. Pero el requisito para sacar el final verdadero es una porquería.
- Con razón se llama xeno crisis, todo lo que jugue y no salio ni un solo seno.

Almost a great game held back by some significant flaws:

1.) drags on a bit too long. This feels like a 35-40 minute game stretched out to ~57 minutes and it really hurts the pacing. The levels go on a bit too long which gets repetitive and grindy feeling which is not what you want in a game like this. Needed 1-2 more levels or simply trimmed down to remove 10-20 minutes.  A great arcade game understands this is the LAST type of game you want to pad the length, as arcade games are meant to be replayed. 

2.) ammo system is a little questionable. The game automatically generates ammo when you begin to get low, forcing the player to go retrieve it. It works, but makes the ammo system feel a little moot. I get that the point is make the player make a risk to get to the ammo, but something about it seems a little strange.

3.) Questionable roll system. you’re nearly invincible when rolling, and rolls have no cooldown meaning you can chain them. Yes, you can still take damage, if you roll into a really bad spot, but often times it feels overly strong and makes certain bosses and rooms/enemy types feel completely invalidated by your ability to roll as you completely dodge bullets during the entire roll. It’s just a bit questionable to have a bullet-immune dodge with no recovery or cooldown in this kind of game. 

4.) final boss is complete garbage even on hard. No seriously, it’s pathetically easy and terribly designed. You can stand in 1 corner and do nothing, wait for the vulnerable area to show, rinse and repeat with zero challenge. Extremely disappointing ending to a game that otherwise puts up a decent challenge. 

5.) contrary to some other comments, the game is actually too easy even on hard when you realize how strong rolling is and know how to parse your end of level upgrades: first fully upgrade fire power, then health, then everything else. 

6.) not really much replay value. There is an infinity mode after clearing the game which adds a nice touch of replayability. The boss rush is ok, but the bosses are not particularly captivating enough to make much difference in replayability.  After beating hard, there feels like little reason to do anything but infinite mode, which is a good pick up and play mode, but it’s also bite sized without much meat on it, just 1 tiny level, play til you die.  The main campaign is not particularly fun to replay after beating due to point #1. 

7.) difficulty peaks at level 5, the last 2 stages are easier which hurts the game’s pacing and sense of progression and also makes the game too easy. 

&.) enemies can spawn on you occasionally leading to cheap hits. This is a commonly cited issue and it’s frustrating the devs never fixed this or didn’t invest enough time into polishing the game fully before releasing it to so many systems. Especially because they’ve known for years this issue and has been brought up by many players. 
———————
If these were fixed, and added some other end game type challenge to keep a player more hooked, it would be great. The aesthetic, responsiveness and tight  gameplay feel is good and makes me WANT to like it, but it’s just held back by the above flaws.  Because there’s not much meat or content to the game in general, unfortunately these flaws overshadow the experience, leaving little more joy to glean after clearing the game once.  6-10$ is a more reasonable price in that sense. I can’t recommend it at more than that price.

Xeno Crisis é um jogo com forte influências de fliperamas como Smash TV. A dificuldade é alta e é recomendado jogar no modo fácil para aprender as manhas antes de tentar o difícil. A diferença entre os dois é que no fácil há continues logo de cara, a munição da arma principal é mais farta e os inimigos têm menos vida. Mesmo assim, o jogo continua com um bom desafio. 

A temática do jogo não faz questão alguma de esconder que foi baseada em Aliens: O Resgate, pelo menos no início, por causa do tipo de monstros com quem você luta na primeira fase. Há uma variedade legal de inimigos, e eles vêm numa cadência perfeita, nunca te deixando construir uma zona de conforto para si. 

Apesar de ser um jogo desenvolvido com a ideia de ser lançado para uma gama enorme de plataformas, do Mega Drive ao Dreamcast e todos os outros no meio e depois, Xeno Crisis é um dos mais lindos jogos em pixel art que eu já joguei. É incrível saber que é praticamente a mesma experiência em todos os ports, do mais fraco tecnologicamente ao PlayStation 4 ou 5 da vida.

Fiquei surpreso com a qualidade da jogabilidade também. Mesmo sendo um jogo no estilo clássico, bem arcade, ele tem uma certa complexidade, tanto na movimentação quanto na variedade de armas. Algumas, por exemplo, acabam sendo mais úteis em determinadas situações do que outras, sem falar na sempre útil faquinha, praquelas horas em que a caca bate no ventilador. 

Em suma, Xeno Crisis é um dos jogos retrô que mais valem a pena serem jogados hoje em dia. É de uma qualidade absurda, trazendo muita diversão por um preço decente, ainda mais durante as muitas promoções do Steam. Peguei por 10 reais e não me arrependo!

Meine Review zu "Xeno Crisis":

"Xeno Crisis" ist ein klassischer Arcade-Twin-Stick-Shooter der vom Titel her schon an das bekannte "ALIEN"-Franchise angelehnt ist. 
Das Gameplay ist richtig Flott unterwegs und leicht erklärt. Man wählt einen weiblichen oder männlichen Soldaten aus und schon wird man auf einen Alien-Verseuchten Planeten abgesetzt um diesen von den blutrünstigen Kreaturen zu säubern. Dabei sieht man die einzelnen Areale bzw. Kammern stets von oben die auch immer nur einen Bildschirm groß sind, ist dieses Areal von schleimigen Biestern gesäubert öffnen sich eine oder mehrere Türen und man kommt zur nächsten Gegnerwelle, so lange bis man zum Level-Boss geschleust wird der dann ordentlich mit allerlei Bewaffnung eingedeckt werden darf. 
Erlegt man diesen jeweiligen Level-Boss kann man die eingesammelten Hundemarken/ Dog Tags gegen verschieden Skillpunkte eintauschen, wie z.B. mehr Munition, Waffenstärke usw. und schon geht es ab ins nächste Gebiet. Ich bin persönlich nur bis zum 4. Level gekommen, da ich viel zu oft unnötig in Projektiele oder in die Feinde selbst hineinlaufe und so Wertvolle Leben verliere...also menschliches Versagen würde ich da mal sagen. ^^'
Das Game ist schon relativ knackig in seiner Schwierigkeit, es gibt den Standard-Modus der von Hause aus schon "Schwierig" heißt und einen Leichten Modus. Aber da das Gameplay so Flott ist und die Motivationsspirale gut zündet, erwischt man sich schnell wie man immer und immer noch einen Durchlauf startet und sich den außerirdischen Gesindel mit Waffengewalt in den Weg stellt!
Achso, noch kurz ein paar technische Aspekte: Die Grafik ist Wunderbar Retro, aber nicht hässlich, sondern im charmanten Pixel-Look dargestellt, die Musik treibt einen zusätzlich durch die Areale - Toll! :D 

Ich habe mir das Game im Sale geholt und dafür ist der Preis dann auch in Ordnung!
Also wer kurzweilige, knackige Arcade-Action in Retro-Look haben will, ist bei "Xeno Crisis" an der richtigen Adresse und darf den Adrenalin-Rausch in vollen Zügen genießen! :)

Xeno Crisis is a retro modern arcade style twin-stick shooter ultimately made to run on the Sega Genesis.  Fortunately, there's a Steam version.

Xeno Crisis is a pretty straight forward game. With most modern controllers that have two sticks, one moves the character in different directions.  While the other aims the character's weapon in one of eight directions.  Which may not make a lot of sense at first since the character's movement is so fluid, but their shooting is so locked down.  However, plug in a USB Sega Genesis (preferably a 6/8 button one) controller and the weapon aiming makes more sense.  Though, it doesn't become any easier to aim. The buttons become how the player aims their character's shots.  Either way, it does take a little getting used to.     

In addition to shooting, the player has grenades that detonate on contact with enemies or go off after a couple of seconds.  Either way, it does more damage and in an area of effect.  Other than that, the player character can roll to avoid damage, but care has to be taken where the roll lands the character.

All weapons are limited resources in Xeno Crisis.  Including the default assault rifle.  This may catch some players out their first run and seem like a drawback at first compared to other twin-stick shooters like Smash TV.  However, Xeno Crisis doesn't seem to have the massive hordes of enemies swarming to you.  And with unlimited ammo, I think it'd be too easy to ABS (always be shooting) and control the play area.  The game seems to provide enough ammo as long as the player refrains from spraying and praying.  And even when completely out of bullets or close up, the player character has a fairly strong melee attack.

In addition to the default assault rifle and grenades, the player can pick up various weapons.  Such as shotguns, laserguns, spread shot, rocket launchers and even a BFG.  These weapons are notably more powerful, but you'll quickly run out of ammo for them.  Some enemies drop dog tags.  These can be exchanged at the end of a stage for upgrades such as more health, stronger shooting and even more continues.

And your going to be using your continues pretty often as you learn to play this game.  Xeno Crisis isn't easy, even on the Easy.  The game has two difficulty settings, Hard and Easy.  And as far as I can tell the difference is largely in the number of item drops and maybe a few less hits to put enemies down.  Either way, the game isn't a cake walk.

The graphics, music and sound are all very Sega Genesis.  I love the graphics of the Genesis, and I think the sound of the console often gets a bad rep.  Zeno Crisis does a good job with both video and audio.  Especially like the game's choice of colors.

It's hard for me to not recommend Xeno Crisis, as the Genesis is my favorite console and twin stick shooters have been a favorite of mine since Robotron 2084.  Xeno Crisis feels like something from the early to mid 90s on the Genesis.  Which can be good or bad depending on if you want something that looks retro but plays modern or want something that feels like it was locked in a time capsule and just unearthed.

Ignore my play time, since I've put about a dozen hours into this game on Xbox game pass. For some reason I still bought it, but I regret that now.
I love Smash TV and I hate it when people compare this game to that one. I really wish someone would make an updated Smash TV, because this isn't it. 
Smash has you on an intergalactic violent TV show mowing down hordes of enemies and collecting tons of cash and prizes. Items and power-ups were everywhere, and it took a while to get bored playing it. The entire experience was fun and exciting. The game played far more basic than this one, and the only main difference is really the theme of the two games, but I'm still fond of Smash TV twenty years later.
Enter Xenocrisis which people claim is as good as Smash. Xenocrisis has you going room to room gunning down mostly the same aliens over and over with limited ammo for your main gun, forcing you to use a comically garbage and damn near useless melee attack. That's it.
The only similarities between this and Smash TV are that they are both room to room arena shooters.
It all feels generic; weapons, power ups, and enemies. There's nothing new here that hasn't been seen a hundred times before in countless numbers of games.
There's barely any reason to replay this. 
The two "characters" are literally gender palette swapped mirror images of each other.
Enemies layer over top of each other, they spawn right on top of you, they are repetitive as all unholy hell, there's nowhere near enough pickups and variety to keep it interesting, and personally I got bored of it all real quick.
"Randomised" room layout, with the general order of progression being exactly the same every time. It's only the illusion of random, and a goofy parlour trick at best.
Enemy bullets are way to hard to see, and this results in taking several cheap hits which could have been easily dodged.
Even despite all of this, the game could still be playable if it wasn't for it's greatest flaw: enemies that spawn directly beneath you, or fall on your head with no warning. This is the ultimate game design flaw, and I assume the only reason the developer left it this way is to add artificial difficulty.
If you're going to mimic a classic game, it should be at least as good as the game it wants to imitate, if not better. Otherwise there's no point, and we get games like Xenocrisis.
I'd recommend picking it up for a couple bucks if you really want to check it out, but I paid five dollars and even that's too much for what you get.

If I were to summarise Xeno Crisis I'd call it an Arcade, Run and Gun, Twin Stick shooter with a high level of difficulty. The Difficulty is part of the experience but your move set is built to rise to that challenge as long as you can master the skill ceiling provided for your abilities.

You start the game choosing between two characters, while character stats are not revealed until you get to an upgrade screen at the end of each level there are some minor differences in their game play. The male protagonist 'John Marsh' has slightly more starting ammunition compared to 'Sarah Ridley' who has a faster movement speed instead to avoid enemy attacks. Beyond that, all their stats are the same and you can purchase upgrades by collecting dog tags to gradually customise their play style.

As Xeno Crisis has an arcade feel, the plot is only surface level with reliance on some favoured tropes to the sci-fi action genre it is paying homage to; Space Marines, BFG weapons, Xenomorph-lite monsters and other pop-culture tropes dot the levels. There is a good and bad ending, though I will admit I have not been able to get either - the latter levels in my experience became incredibly difficult to the point I would have considered  it gruelling even with a cheat for infinite lives available. I'd say play this for some arcade style fun and see how far your limited selection of lives will take you.

Beyond the Initial Arcade Mode there is an Infinite and Boss Rush mode available, all you have to do is press and hold a selection of buttons on the main menu before initialising a one or two player game. There is also a Cheat and Backer menu that can be accessed via similar means.

The only other thing I have left to describe is the presentation. I'm a fan of pixel art graphics and I'd say this looks particularly good and the soundtrack kicks along with headbanging tunes too. It is a technical marvel for the hardware limitations it was designed for (the Sega Mega Drive) and the fact that the developers have put this game on physical cartridges for the Mega Drive as well as the Neo Geo, Dreamcast and Arcade Machines! it amazes me when people can build games with such polish for older hardware that isn't commonly in use.

So yeah, Xeno Crisis is definitely a game with a lot of style and presentation. Its arcade action through and through so if you don't mind the difficulty and just want to shoot aliens with a killer soundtrack blasting away, I'd say go get it!

7.5/10
